title: What is where in the on-module eMMC

steps.title: An eMMC is three storage areas in one chip
steps.body: The SD card on top is the reference. Below it the eMMC has two boot partitions, a user area and a small replay-protected area. Each has its own name in Linux and in U-Boot.

steps.title: The SD layout, for comparison
steps.body: `imx-boot.bin` at 32 KiB, a saved U-Boot environment at 7 MiB and the root partition from 8 MiB. The same bytes go into the eMMC user area when you flash the image there.

steps.title: boot0: where the ROM looks when told to
steps.body: A 4 MiB hardware partition, `/dev/mmcblk2boot0`, selected in U-Boot with `mmc dev 2 1`. `imx-boot.bin` goes in at byte 0, not at 32 KiB. Linux keeps boot partitions read-only unless you write `0` to `/sys/block/mmcblk2boot0/force_ro`.

steps.title: boot1: the second copy
steps.body: `./build.sh uuu emmc` writes the same container here. The ROM only boots the partition named in `PARTITION_CONFIG`, so boot1 is a spare that a later update can switch to.

steps.title: The user area: partitions and the OS
steps.body: Here sit the MBR, the root filesystem as `/dev/mmcblk2p1`, and U-Boot's saved environment at 7 MiB. The partition is only as large as the image, so grow it once on the board.

steps.anchor: copy, unused while boot0 is on
steps.title: The 32 KiB copy is a leftover
steps.body: It comes with the SD image. While boot0 is enabled the ROM ignores it. It becomes the boot image again if you set `BOOT_PARTITION_ENABLE` back to 0.

steps.title: Why the environment is erased
steps.body: A saved environment (`saveenv`) lives at 7 MiB of the user area and survives a block-mapped re-flash. A full flash zeroes it, so no old `fdt_file` or `bootcmd` is carried over.

steps.anchor: Which area does the ROM read?  EXT_CSD[179] PARTITION_CONFIG, written by  mmc partconf 2 1 1 0
steps.title: One register decides
steps.body: `BOOT_PARTITION_ENABLE` picks boot0, boot1 or the user area. `mmc partconf 2 1 1 0` means: eMMC device 2, boot ack on, boot0, access to the user area. Read it back before you flip the switch.
